- Overestimate prices when sentiment is positive (especially >0.3) and recent prices are rising — model tends to overshoot.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is negative or neutral (especially <0.2) — model fails to capture downward pressure.
- Model consistently overreacts to short-term sentiment spikes, especially when sentiment rises sharply in the last 3–5 days.
- Forecast tends to lag mean reversion — prices often correct downward after model peaks, especially if sentiment drops or stabilizes.
- When sentiment is high but recent price action is flat or slightly declining, model still forecasts upward — overconfidence in sentiment signal.
- Model underestimates volatility in early 2025 (e.g., Jan 2025) — forecasts too smooth, ignoring sharp reversals or sudden drops.
- For 30-day forecasts, model often fails to account for sentiment-driven “sudden shifts” — e.g., sentiment spikes followed by sharp price drops.
- If sentiment is high but price is near recent high, model tends to overpredict — “peak chasing” bias.
- Model underestimates downward corrections after strong upward moves — especially when sentiment drops after a spike.
